title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
gist: At Ignite, Satya Nadella announced general availability of Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he called 'the new OS for work', plus the Copilot Autopilot autonomous agent (billed via Copilot Credits), Microsoft IQ/Work IQ, and expanded Agent 365 governance and spend analytics. Nadella conceded AI models can't be trusted by definition and pitched architectural controls instead, while barely addressing last week's global Exchange/Teams outage.

insights.claim: Microsoft made Word, Excel, and PowerPoint generally available inside Copilot, which Nadella called the new OS for work, letting users create Office files directly in Copilot that remain editable in the Office apps.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Microsoft is repositioning Copilot as the primary interface, defending Office's moat against AI-native rivals.

insights.claim: Microsoft's vision inverts traditional software: agents drive the work while applications become plugin components, backed by an organizational knowledge layer drawing on emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: If apps become agent plugins, value shifts to the agent/context layer owner.
insights.locator: The announcement is a striking inversion

insights.claim: Copilot Autopilot is a persistent, proactive cloud agent to which users delegate responsibilities across email and calendars, billed on usage via Copilot Credits with final pricing not yet announced.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Usage-based billing shifts Microsoft's AI monetization toward consumption; watch pricing.

insights.claim: Microsoft IQ, now generally available, houses Work IQ, a context layer that Nadella described as perhaps a company's most valuable database of people, relationships, and work artifacts.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Proprietary enterprise graph data is Microsoft's strategic lock-in asset.
insights.locator: Also announced as generally available at

insights.claim: Copilot Workspaces, in the Frontier early-access program, aims to make AI multiplayer with people and agents sharing context, with personal Autopilot agents coming to Workspaces soon.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Collaborative agents broaden seat expansion potential.
insights.quote: Workspaces makes it a truly multiplayer experience

insights.claim: Nadella conceded that alignment and mechanistic understanding of AI models remain elusive and that, by definition, such powerful technology can't be trusted.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Rare CEO admission reframes enterprise AI risk; governance tooling becomes a sales lever.
insights.quote: The question is: How can you even trust all this powerful technology? The reality is, by definition, you can’t,

insights.claim: Microsoft's answer is an architectural separation of intelligence from authority: each Autopilot agent gets a unique ID, admins can restrict or block it, all activities are logged, and agents can request human approval.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Identity/permissions for agents is a growth area in enterprise security.
insights.locator: In a departure from the norms

insights.claim: The author notes Microsoft is asking businesses to trust its own safeguards instead, whose effectiveness against mistakes, rogue actions, or data exposure is yet to be demonstrated.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Agent adoption depends on unproven controls; watch for incidents.
insights.locator: The promised agent controls and admission

insights.claim: Microsoft's AI Transparency Initiative partners with 40-plus companies including Adobe and MasterCard to develop open AI governance and security standards.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Standard-setting can entrench Microsoft's governance approach.
insights.locator: Along with the guardrails, Microsoft announced

insights.claim: Agent 365 Business Analytics, which Nadella called an ERP system of AI usage, will show customers AI token-spend costs versus value of work performed.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Enterprises are demanding AI ROI measurement; tools that justify spend support renewals.
insights.quote: “You can simply think of this as an ERP system of AI usage.

insights.claim: Microsoft acknowledged that Agent 365's assisted-work-hour estimates are generated by a model rather than measured directly, a telling concession as businesses question AI ROI.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: AI productivity claims remain modeled, not measured; skepticism on ROI is warranted.
insights.locator: Customers will be able to see

insights.claim: Microsoft Commercial Business CEO Judson Althoff claimed anything done with Claude or ChatGPT can be done better with Copilot for less.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Microsoft is competing on price against Anthropic and OpenAI in enterprise.
insights.quote: “anything you can do with Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot, for less.”

insights.claim: Nadella gave only a brief acknowledgment of last week's global outage disrupting Exchange Online and Teams, saying Microsoft has work to do.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Reliability concerns rise as Microsoft asks customers to grant agents more autonomy.
insights.quote: “Last week was a reminder of how critical digital infrastructure is as the dial tone for the world,”

insights.claim: Microsoft highlighted its community-first AI infrastructure plan, seemingly acknowledging growing public concern over data center projects.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Local opposition to data centers is a capex execution risk.
insights.locator: That statement was all the time
